next_step: Finalize Dedicated commit tiers + legal review of SLA and data residency addendum
notes: Company background: product-led mid-market B2B SaaS (workflow automation for SMB accounting teams). Heavy emphasis on low-latency chat for customer support and fast vector search across 10M+ docs.

Initial engagement: interested in Redwood hosted API for quick integration to validate model quality (chat + reranking). Completed hosted POC Feb 2-16; results: good relevance on reranker, average latency 110ms for short chats, cost higher than expected at current qps.
Decision pivot: after hosted POC they requested Dedicated evaluation to get predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale. Concerned about cold-start and KV cache persistence during restarts.

Technical constraints: must support SSO (SAML), enterprise audit logs, customer-managed KMS, and optional data residency in us-east-1. On-prem not required but VPC peering mandatory for Dedicated control plane.

Traffic profile: peak qps ~800 small chat requests (prompt 80-150 tokens) during US business hours; background embedding jobs for nightly indexing (~200k vectors/day). Latency SLO: 150ms p95 for chat; target p95 80-100ms desirable.
Cost sensitivity: mid-market procurement — wants predictability for budgeting; open to commit with ramp but needs clear burst and overage math (finance will sign only with 3-month ramp guarantee).
Quote from CTO on demo: 'Need to see 30% cost delta vs hosted at our expected 6-month runrate to justify Dedicated spend.'
Procurement notes: legal flagged KMS language and encryption at rest SLA; security wants SOC2 Type 2 evidence and audit log retention options (90/365 days).
SE notes: Maya set up Dedicated proof-of-architecture (POA) slide deck and a proposed canary rollout plan. Presented two commit options on 2026-03-03 call (see pricing_negotiation_summary).
Next immediate actions: finalize commit tiers, provide pro forma SOW, legal to review KMS addendum, schedule on-site/network verification (if required).

pricing_negotiation_summary: Two primary commit proposals presented on 2026-03-03. Option A (conservative ramp): Month1 commit $12k (25% baseline), Month2 $24k (50%), Month3 $36k (75%), Month4 $48k (100%) -> 12-month term, 2x burst allowance, overage charged at 1.5x committed rate. Option B (aggressive discount): Flat monthly commit $40k with 3-month ramp credit and 3x burst at reduced overage 1.25x committed rate; requires upfront 6-month payment or bank guarantee. Finance leaning to Option A due to cashflow constraints.
commit_proposal: Option A - Ramp (recommended by AE): 12-month term, starting commit $12k/mo (25% of target), ramp to $48k/mo by month 4; burst up to 2x on short bursts (subject to capacity) at no additional commitment; overage billed at 1.5x committed unit price; SLA 99.5% for inference nodes.

Option B - Flat/Discount: 12-month term, flat commit $40k/mo, 3x burst for emergency, overage 1.25x; requires 6 months prepaid or signed enterprise PO with payment schedule. Includes 90-day accelerated support and onboarding assistance.
burst_policy_proposal: Burst allowed up to 2x baseline for Option A (soft guarantees) and up to 3x for Option B (hard burst SLA when prepaid). Bursts will be throttled based on node availability; Redwood will provide telemetry for burst events and billing spikes.
overage_terms: Overage invoiced monthly with line-item showing committed units vs usage. Rate multiplier applied to unit price (1.5x Option A; 1.25x Option B). Credit policy: if sustained overage >30% for 2 consecutive months, Redwood will offer an amendment to move to higher commit tier with prorated credits.
ramp_schedule: Customer requests 3-month visible ramp for budget sign-off: month1 25% commit, month2 50%, month3 75%, month4 full. Redwood suggested 4-month ramp to give time for KV cache warmup and traffic shaping. Finance needs monthly invoices aligned to ramp steps.
